title: Glitchy
text: Waste of a dollar.  Every time I inadvertently tipped my iPhone4 into landscape mode, and then uprighted it, the program display would get all screwed up--as if I had zoomed in to see just the lower left part of the display.  And it would remain that way until I killed the program and restarted.  Very annoying.  Crashed once as well.  Deleted and wrote it off as a loss.  However, when it worked it seemed OK.  Plain, easy to read meter, quick response, etc. FWIW.

title: No gods after upgrade!!!
text: This ap worked perfectly until the last "upgrade".  From what I can see, the only thing this change did was add a commercial for an expensive, external microphone while taking away the ability to adjust the "MAX" signal level.  It really is a shame to see them mess up a nice ap try and get you to pay them more money.  I used to rate this as a five star ap, now I'm going to delete it if it's not fixed.  Very disappointed!

title: Good for basics after tweeks
text: I bought this app to properly set the levels on my new home theater. By default the readings were way low in comparison with my RadioShack meter. After tweaking the trim extensively it matches up pretty well. However even when calibrated and using c weight and slow response my iPhone 4s with this app was completely incapable of picking up my subwoofer test tone for subwoofer level setting.

title: SPL Not Consistent
text: Does not give consistent readings.  Varies by 10 to 20 dB.  Does not alway turn on when app is touched, have to tap fast/slow button to get to start.

title: Dosent
text: Not able to identify my sub-woofer. I'm using iphone 4s for this app & when I play my sub-woofer for configuration this meter sits ideal.

title: Not bad for basic home use
text: The db knob is way to touchy. A three point calibration would be beneficial, as it is not accurate at all. I calibrated it on my iPhone4 at 85db. At 115db it indicates 96 and at 45db it indicates 58. These test were done using a professionally calibrated meter.

title: Meh!
text: I was hoping this meter would measure bass but it doesnt. Very dissapointed. But for .99 can't really complain. lol

title: Neat but...
text:
Well I don't know how accurate it is. Seemed to max out at around 90db with internal mic. Don't have an external. 
One thing that is annoying is the round scale knob. It seems to be be very touchy and a pain to set it to a value. 

Running on 4g iPod touch.

title: Useless with ipod touch and blue mikey v1
text: If you try to use this with an ipod touch and a blue mikey, all you get is screeching horrible feedback.  No option to turn off playback/mic.  Completely and utterly useless.

title: It crashes!
text: After downloading latest update it simply crashes!  I liked it before this.

title: Was loving it...
text: Was loving it on iPad, but now that it crashes, I cannot tell if I love it.

title: A "Sound" App! :)
text:
Working as a sound tech with some friends, a buddy got this app and we compared it to a "real" decibel-meter. It was about 10 dB off, but then a quick calibration brought it in to be accurate. Will prove very helpful as we travel venues and locales. P.S. To the guy who gave it 1-star, I would ask if you don't know what the controls are for, you don't know what this is really used for...why rate the app low for YOUR lack of understanding?

2.7: has a bug. if you flip phone so speakers an micro pointed up, you can only see the bottom corner of the app.

title: review
text:
this is ok, is not great. with loud sound it does a little better then with low sound. When using with low sound it way off, i mean 10+ dBs off. But for the price, what can you ask.
